mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuthBoundary allows Operations whose caller is Unauthenticated to exist in the model, directly violating FR-001 and the AuthRequiredEverywhere pattern predicate.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBoundaryViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller = Unauthenticated }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AppendOnlyDeletionLog lets two distinct TaskDeletion atoms share the same loggedRef, meaning the same task appears twice in the deletion log — exactly the duplication the AppendOnly predicate is supposed to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj d1, d2: TaskDeletion | d1.loggedRef = d2.loggedRef }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_ClosedTaskEditRule allows an EditOp to target a Done task without supplying a non-Done newStatus (i.e., newStatus is empty or Done), which is exactly the closed-task violation FR-011 prohibits.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskViolation { some e: EditOp | e.targetTask.status = Done and no e.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_PermanentDeletion allows a LiveTask to share its taskRef with a TaskDeletion loggedRef, meaning a 'deleted' task still appears as a live task — violating the permanent-deletion invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermanentDeletionViolation { some t: LiveTask, d: TaskDeletion | t.taskRef = d.loggedRef }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuditCompleteness allows a TaskDeletion to exist with no corresponding DeleteOperation, meaning a deletion was logged but no operation ever triggered it — breaking the completeness invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some d: TaskDeletion | no dop: DeleteOperation | dop.auditEntry = d }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_DeleteOpAttribution allows a DeleteOperation whose auditEntry.deleter differs from its own caller, or whose auditEntry.loggedRef differs from deletedRef — a mis-attribution in the deletion log that AttributionCorrectness is designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some dop: DeleteOperation | dop.auditEntry.deleter != dop.caller }
